definition: Ominous means serving as a sign that trouble is coming — foreshadowing evil the way a dark omen does.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ominous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ominous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The letter's ominous closing line — 'we will speak of this again soon' — kept the inspector awake half the night.
Unsettling is milder than ominous: an unsettling detail stirs a vague unease, while an ominous one points to specific trouble on the way.
Menacing is stronger than ominous — the ominous merely signals danger to come, while the menacing is the danger itself, present and aimed at you.
Foreboding most often names the feeling — the heavy inner sense that something bad is coming. Ominous belongs to the sign itself: the sky, the silence, the letter that carries the warning.
Threatening implies an actor: someone or something intends the harm and shows it. Ominous needs no intender — a barometer reading can be ominous; it merely predicts, the way an omen does.

Ominous belongs precisely to that interval — it names the sign, not the disaster, and claims only that the sign points toward trouble.
The moment the mountain actually blows, the pattern stops being ominous and becomes a catastrophe's first chapter.
Ominous attaches to things that are read — skies, silences, footsteps, closing lines — and claims they predict trouble.
Where a person means you harm, reach for threatening or menacing; where the signs simply point the wrong way, ominous is the word.
Its bright opposite is auspicious, the omen read for good.

The observatory's job was to read a mountain that could not speak.
For three quiet years the instruments recorded almost nothing: a tremor here, a wisp of steam there, the ordinary breathing of a sleeping volcano.
In March the readings changed.
The lake on the crater floor warmed by two degrees, and the tremors began arriving in rhythmic swarms.
None of this endangered anyone yet, and the mountain intended nothing — mountains never do.
But to the monitoring team the pattern was ominous, an unmistakable sign that an eruption was assembling itself below.
They did not wait for smoke.
The evacuation notices went out that same week, drafted calmly, before the danger itself had even arrived.
